summary: Frontend E2E validation of the new sudden-death Tie-Breaker feature. Ran a full multi-context Playwright flow with 1 admin + 3 student browser sessions. All 7 required scenarios PASSED: (1) fire rejected with <2 selected -> correct toast 'Select at least 2 tied finalists', (2) firing switches admin to live view with clear-tiebreaker button, (3) participant students see tiebreaker-card on /dashboard with question + input + Lock In and card shows 'Answer locked' after submit (submit button removed, second submission prevented client-side by not rendering), (4) admin live view shows both participants with Correct/Wrong badges, answer text, timestamp, and 'fastest correct' marker on Alice, (5) declare-winner-{id} works, admin shows tb-resolved and student S1 sees 'You won the tie-breaker!' while S2 sees 'The tie-breaker has been decided.', (6) clear-tiebreaker returns admin to create form and removes card from student dashboard within poll cycle, (7) non-participant student S3 never saw the tiebreaker-card. Post-test cleanup executed: DELETE /api/tiebreaker, POST /api/rounds/reset, and the 3 test students deleted via /api/students/{id}.
critical_code_review_comments: Dashboard.jsx TieBreakerCard visibility check `if (!tb || !tb.active && !tb.resolved) return null;` relies on JS operator precedence (evaluated as `!tb || (!tb.active && !tb.resolved)`). Works today but is easy to break; wrap with explicit parentheses for readability.

Admin.jsx TieBreakerTab load() -> `data.active === false && !data.id ? null : data` collapses the non-active empty state, but if backend ever returns a stale tb with active=false and id set (e.g. resolved but not cleared), the admin would still see the resolved view — acceptable, but consider explicit `resolved` flag.

Backend answer_tiebreaker uses `$push` without a concurrency guard; two very-close submissions from the same student in a race could double-push. Consider `$addToSet` on student_id or a conditional update `{'responses.student_id': {'$ne': uid}}`.

Backend declare_tiebreaker sets overall_winner=true but does NOT reset any previous overall_winner flag on the previously-declared student if the same tie-breaker is re-declared or a new tie-breaker overrides — could yield multiple overall_winners over time. Consider clearing prior overall_winner on declare.

Backend clear_tiebreaker only $unsets the doc; it does not roll back overall_winner/round_wins:3 for the previously declared winner. If admin declares by mistake then Clear, the student stays overall_winner. Consider undoing on clear before winner is finalised, or add an explicit 'undo declare' endpoint.
server.py at 583 lines with mixed concerns (auth, competition, tiebreaker) — still recommend splitting into routers as flagged in iteration_1.

rca of the issue: No functional issues found in the tie-breaker feature; all scenarios behaved as specified. Only advisory concerns are around (a) declare/clear not reversing overall_winner side-effects and (b) minor race window in the answer $push. Neither blocks the current MVP.
